items.title: Sepsis and Septic Shock
highYieldSummary: Recognize infection with organ dysfunction or shock physiology using an early structured assessment.
Obtain appropriate cultures and investigations without delaying time-critical treatment or source control.
Use repeated perfusion, mental-status, respiratory, and urine-output assessment to guide resuscitation.
Escalate early when hypotension, rising lactate, respiratory failure, or deterioration persists.
examPearls: The trajectory and perfusion matter more than a single screening score.
examTraps: Do not wait for a complete workup before treating a deteriorating patient.
items.arabicExplanation: الإنتان حالة ديناميكية. ابحث عن خلل الأعضاء والتروية، ابدأ التقييم والعلاج مبكرًا، وأعد الفحص بعد كل تدخل مع معالجة مصدر العدوى.

items.title: Acute Stroke Assessment
highYieldSummary: Establish the last-known-well time, glucose, airway and vital stability, anticoagulant exposure, and baseline function.
Use focused neurologic examination and urgent brain and vascular imaging according to the current local stroke pathway.
Consider reperfusion eligibility and hemorrhage management in parallel with supportive care and specialist activation.
Reassess for mimics such as hypoglycemia, seizure, migraine, toxicologic states, and systemic illness.
examTraps: Do not label a deficit as a stroke without checking glucose and common mimics.
items.arabicExplanation: الوقت عنصر علاجي. وثّق آخر وقت كان فيه المريض طبيعيًا، افحص السكر، فعّل مسار السكتة، واستبعد النزف والمقلدات بالتوازي.

items.title: Initial Evaluation of Major Trauma
highYieldSummary: Use a team-based primary survey with immediate treatment of threats to airway, breathing, circulation, disability, and exposure.
Control catastrophic hemorrhage early and repeat the primary survey after every major intervention or change.
Use mechanism, physiology, examination, and focused imaging to select operative, interventional, or nonoperative pathways.
Coordinate transfer, blood products, specialist activation, analgesia, warming, and documentation as one resuscitation plan.
examPearls: A normal initial blood pressure does not exclude major hemorrhage.
examTraps: Do not let a distracting injury delay the primary survey.
items.arabicExplanation: في الرضوض الكبيرة ابدأ بالمسح الأولي وعالج النزف ومشكلات مجرى الهواء والتنفس فورًا. أعد المسح بعد كل تدخل ولا تسمح لإصابة ظاهرة أن تشتت الانتباه.

items.title: Approach to the Poisoned Patient
highYieldSummary: Stabilize the patient first and obtain a time-based exposure history, including formulation, amount, co-ingestants, and intent.
Use toxidrome recognition, glucose, temperature, ECG, acid-base status, and targeted levels to identify immediately dangerous patterns.
Contact a poison center or toxicology service early for agent-specific treatment and observation guidance.
Avoid routine decontamination or antidotes without a plausible indication and a benefit-risk assessment.
examPearls: The ECG is a core toxicology test in an undifferentiated ingestion.
examTraps: Do not rely on a negative screening panel to exclude poisoning.
items.arabicExplanation: ثبّت المريض أولًا ثم اجمع قصة التعرض بدقة. تخطيط القلب والسكر والحرارة والحماض تساعد في كشف السموم الخطرة، واستشر مركز السموم مبكرًا.

items.title: Acute Abdominal Pain
highYieldSummary: Start with hemodynamic stability, pain severity, pregnancy possibility, surgical history, medications, and red-flag features.
Keep time-critical diagnoses in the differential while using focused examination, laboratory tests, and imaging to answer specific questions.
Provide analgesia and antiemetic therapy while continuing diagnostic reassessment; symptom treatment does not remove the need to search for dangerous causes.
Choose disposition based on physiology, diagnostic certainty, response, social safety, and reliable follow-up.
examPearls: Pain severity alone does not predict disease severity.
examTraps: Do not dismiss serious disease because the initial examination is benign.
items.arabicExplanation: ألم البطن يحتاج تقييم الاستقرار والحمل والعمليات السابقة وعلامات الخطر. أعطِ المسكنات مع استمرار البحث عن الأسباب الخطيرة وإعادة الفحص.
